reason: The I1a run showed a repeatable ticket workflow: per-step reporting with op=step, closing with op=done, leaving stacked spec amendments for a separate pass when siblings edit the same record, and correcting a memory the change made false. No existing skill states these.

Working this ticket from a dispatched agent surfaced an environment trap: inherited identity variables made a worker's test writes refused, and a seeded fixture broke an equality assertion. Both are predictable for the next ticket that touches authority or test fixtures, so the ticket-work skill should carry them.

A single-quoted memory payload containing "tickets'" was cut at the apostrophe, so the CLI rejected the JSON and the shell ran the remainder as a command. The heredoc form succeeded on retry. Recording it avoids the same failed write.

A probe with a guessed observation string deleted a still-true observation; the tool said "Observations deleted successfully", so the mistake was only caught afterwards and needed a restore. The rule to read the exact text first, and never delete as a probe, prevents this.

The worker built a feature whose prompt wording was the owner's to accept, outside this ticket's decisions. It shipped the element empty so the feature is off by default, left the ticket open, and recorded the pending draft in the note. That pattern avoids silently inventing owner wording and avoids closing a ticket with an unresolved decision.

The agent guessed the help syntax wrong, then parsed labeled map output by hand, and passed a JSON object where the memory tool expected a list. It also ended its turn with five reader agents outstanding and the ticket note unchanged, though the skill says to edit the note when stopping with the ticket open. The skill is the one in play, so the fix belongs here.

During the source pass the agent read each element with `metaform map where ... full=true` and needed to see what memory already sat at each node before recording its own. The output shape (key: json lines, memory as entities with observations) was only discovered by inspection; the skill tells the next agent to check existing observations first so nodes do not accumulate duplicates.

The source-pass ticket tells the agent to run the codebase-memory CLI with a raw JSON argument; the CLI answered with a deprecation warning on that form and listed the flag and file alternatives. A worker following this skill will hit the same warning, so the skill should name the flag form it should use.

A join id was tried as a map where address and returned nothing (Bash completed with no output). The working route is the element's provides line or map work receiver/provider; recording this saves the dead lookup.
The source-pass procedure now lives in this skill, so the trigger should name it; otherwise an agent assigned a source-pass ticket would not match the skill.

Source-pass tickets recur across elements (sibling tickets for storage, api, interface and this server pass are open), and the procedure for recording seams and gaps currently lives only in each ticket's task text. Holding it at class level means the next pass starts from the rule. Reader-brief and held-gap rules come from what this episode did and what the ticket required.

A source pass in this episode wrote six join seams with this command. The format (JSON value, refs as key/value pairs, full qn names) had to be worked out by trial, and the held-gap rule in the skill does not say how the seam is written.

The worker role refused held-gap writes in this episode, so the skill's instruction to open held work at the join cannot be followed by a dispatched source-pass agent. The working fallback (note on the ticket) was found by the agent at run time and should be the documented route.

In the episode the worker agent attempted `map work op=add ... held=true` three times before reading the refusal and falling back to the ticket note. The skill already says workers cannot open held work but does not say the role check should come first, nor that sources items and memory still work for workers. The add-item and create_entities calls in the same run succeeded from the worker role.

The orchestrator re-read the cited lines of two reader-claimed gaps (loader listeners, move-to-doing skipping the claim check) before writing them, and both held up. That check should be a standing step in source passes, because reader output is summarized and can cite the wrong range or overstate a gap.

A ticket's cited inputs can be stale: this ticket named src/metaform/nonce.py, which is absent from the tree, and it named STATUS-FOR-CODEX.md and SKIPPED-WORK-ACCOUNTING.md at the repo root when they live under artifacts/swarm-2026-10-11/. Also, a Bash cd persists across calls, so the working directory drifted between steps. Check that each named path exists before relying on it, record a missing one as a stale premise in the step, and use absolute paths for artifact files.

In a research ticket the agent resolved a file the ticket named without a directory and then called it missing. The file was in a subfolder, not at the repo root. The agent also recorded a plan with op=plan and got the ticket back without a visible plan record. Ticket work should resolve named paths by search and read the ticket back after a write before relying on it.

The episode fanned 2,041 pending refactor items out to eight reader agents and planned to apply their placements via `refactor resolve`. The skill has reader-brief rules but nothing on placement batches, validation before apply, or the run-file layout the agent had to reverse-engineer from pipeline.py.

The episode's map memory showed the rule the agent had to rediscover after a subtype-join draft was steered back: deeper parts are ordinary elements with purpose joins. The skill says nothing about this, and a stale intake prompt still teaches the wrong model.

Rich corrected the target for code placements: they attach to the provider element, never a purpose/join record. The existing skill's placement-batch rule does not state the target, so the next remainder pass could repeat the mistake.

A pause killed all eight reader agents before any wrote output, and the relaunch had to be reconstructed. The skill's reader rules do not say to check for surviving output or to resume from the last written item.

The person ruled that root `code` (the artifact root) is an invalid placement for implementation items; the skill's placement-batch rule did not forbid it, and the reader brief and apply script had to be patched mid-run. Future refactor-remainder runs need the rule stated where placements are checked.

Two gaps seen in this ticket: a fix delegated to a background subagent kept the ticket open until its report was read, and a shipped UI change left a spec line (VIEW-039 at 09-viewer.md:591) stale. The rule is the person writes specs, so the ticket carries draft wording instead of an edit.

The episode broke the shared working tree with git stash and pop, against an existing user rule, and it trusted the advertised adapter capability before the recorded session confirmed it. Both belong in the ticket-work skill, which the agent works from.
A worker recorded a memory with a cite list so it can be flagged stale after the fix; the ticket skill's memory section should say to do this.

The live file repeats the memory-citation bullet verbatim (lines 23 and 24). Fold the duplicate into one line so the rule is stated once.
A memory entity without a title is refused, and the refusal only shows after the first try. Record the required title field next to the heredoc rule, and the same heredoc pattern for ticket notes.

An acceptance check that needs a fresh agent session was run from the session that wrote the change, and its older runner refused the new op. The ticket must stay open with that check named as the open step, not closed on the refusal.

During a refactor-remainder ticket the agent sent limit=0 to refactor_pending and got a range error, then limit=100 returned a 632,704-character page that spilled to a file. The skill documents the run folder but not the queue API's paging limits or how to read oversized pages, so the next placement pass would repeat both failures.

The agent on a dispatch ticket added a core environment variable in data/session.py and harness.py, which the ticket's module assignment did not cover, and it widened a shared test stand-in only after an autostart test failed. The durable rule is to surface the chassis decision rather than implement it, and to find stand-ins when a signature changes.
Absorbed into the metaform-development umbrella; full body carried verbatim into references/ticket-work.md.
